Question 1. A T flip-flop follows \(Q_{t+1}=T\oplus Q_t\). What happens when \(T=1\)?

A) The output is always 0

B) The output is always 1

C) The output toggles

D) The output keeps its previous state

Answer: C

Name: [SAMPLE-001] T flip-flop toggle behavior

ID: SAMPLE-001

Explanation: With \(T=1\), \(Q_{t+1}=\overline{Q_t}\).

---

Question 2. Identify the flip-flop described by this characteristic table.

\[
\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline
D & Q_{t+1} \\
\hline
0 & 0 \\
1 & 1 \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]

A) SR flip-flop

B) D flip-flop

C) JK flip-flop

D) T flip-flop

Answer: B

---

Question 3. Which input condition makes an SR flip-flop invalid in the active-high convention?

A) \(S=0, R=0\)

B) \(S=0, R=1\)

C) \(S=1, R=0\)

D) \(S=1, R=1\)

Answer: D
